result:
The System menu now has a **Tile all windows** row right after **Fullscreen**. Build, lint, typecheck and the full JS suite all pass; I haven't tried it in a running shell, since Docker and wp-env were off-limits.

**What changed** (on branch `add/system-menu-tile-all-windows`, nothing committed yet):

- **Menu row** (`src/desktop.ts`): choosing it calls the window manager's existing `tile()`. That already tiles only the current desktop, brings back minimized, maximized and fullscreen windows first, and keeps the grid clear of the dock.
- **Grid rule** (`src/window-manager/geometry.ts`): the old picker put 3 windows in a 2x2 grid with an empty cell. The new rule uses `floor(√n)` rows, with as many windows per row as that takes. So 2 windows go side by side, 3 in thirds, 4 in a 2x2 square, 5 and 6 in 3x2, 7 and 8 in 4x2, 9 in 3x3. On a portrait screen the grid turns on its side.
- **Short last row** (`src/window-manager/arrange.ts`): when the last row has fewer windows (5 windows: 3 on top, 2 below), they now share the full width instead of leaving an empty cell.
- **Docs** (`docs/javascript-reference.md`): this said `tile()` had no UI of its own. It now names the menu row and describes the new grid.
- **Tests** (`tests/vitest/arrange.test.ts`): two added, one for the thirds case and one for the short last row.

**Decision for you:** I changed the shared `tile()` rather than writing a second tiling algorithm. That means workspaces using the `tile` layout (the shipped Learning template) get the new grid too. Also, a plugin that forces a grid through the `os.arrange.tile.dimensions` filter will now see its short last row spread across the full width instead of keeping its cell sizes. If either is unwanted, the menu could get its own function instead.

**Checks run:**
- `npm run build`: passes.
- `npm run lint`: 0 errors; the 28 warnings are all file-length warnings.
- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- `npm run test:js`: 529 files, 6616 tests, all passing.
- PHP checks weren't needed (no PHP touched), and the PHPUnit suite was out of scope.

Following the contributor guide, I haven't committed or opened a PR so you can try it first. No wp-env instance is running for this worktree; `npm run env:start` would bring one up on :8890 (log in with admin / password).
